info.title: AI Assistant API
info.description: An AI assistant that reads your setup and proposes changes for you to approve.

bearerAuth.description: Session token sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the token.

cookieAuth.name: jwt
cookieAuth.description: Session JWT cookie set at sign-in. When present, it takes precedence over the Authorization header.

apiKeyAuth.description: API key sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the key, which starts with tmx_. It acts as the key owner and cannot act as anyone else.

get.summary: Token usage, for the current user or everyone
get.description: Totals for today, 7 and 30 days, then per day, per model and per feature over 30 days. scope=all covers every user and adds a per user breakdown; it needs ai.usage.view_all. offset is the browser's time zone offset in minutes, as getTimezoneOffset gives it, so days are the viewer's own.

403.description: Missing ai.use, scope=all without ai.usage.view_all, or the assistant is off.

get.summary: Whether the AI assistant is available to this user
get.description: Deliberately not behind the AI gate: the frontend calls this to decide whether to render any AI surface at all, and needs a plain answer rather than a 403 when the feature is off.

put.summary: Turn the assistant on or off for the current user
put.description: The same value as the user setting "enabled", for the onboarding step and the panel, which set it outside the settings form. Refused while the assistant is off for the whole server.

403.description: The assistant is off for the whole server.

get.summary: List the user's configured AI providers

403.description: The AI assistant is not enabled.

modelOverrides.description: Per model id, a contextWindow in tokens that replaces what the provider reports.

advanced.description: Optional provider request settings. Null clears them.

modelOverrides.description: Replaces every override. Per model id, a contextWindow in tokens; null or a model left out goes back to what the provider reports.

advanced.description: Replaces every advanced setting. Null clears them.

post.summary: List models for a provider that has not been saved yet
post.description: Lets the add-provider form fill its model picker before the provider exists, so nobody has to go and look up model names by hand.

200.description: Model ids, possibly a curated fallback list.

get.summary: List models available from a provider

502.description: The provider could not be reached.

get.summary: The context window of a provider's models, and where it came from
get.description: For the provider's default model, every model with an override, every model the user has called through it, and any named in models. source is override, provider (reported by the provider), guess (from the model's family) or default (128k). refresh asks the provider again instead of using what it said in the last six hours.

get.summary: List the user's AI conversations
Get one conversation with its messages and proposals

post.summary: Send a message and stream the assistant's reply
post.description: Server-sent events. Emits conversation, token, tool_call, tool_result, proposal, done and error frames.
Re-validates the stored payload and applies it as the approving user, through the same core APIs and plugin services a manual action uses.

400.description: The proposal could not be applied.

post.summary: Record that a run_command proposal was executed in an open terminal
post.description: For the terminal-docked assistant only. The command is typed into the user's already-open SSH session client-side, not re-run over a pooled connection here; this just marks the proposal applied with the output the client captured, so the card and the /apply path stay in sync without running the command twice.

400.description: The proposal is not a run_command proposal, or the hostId does not match.

get.summary: Auto-ops tasks and plans waiting for a decision
get.description: tasks are the user's own, newest first. approvals are proposed plans and plans being run that the user may decide on: their own, and everyone's for a holder of ai.ops.use.

403.description: Missing ai.use, or the assistant is off.

get.summary: The provider, model and language the user's tasks use

put.summary: Save the provider, model and language for the user's tasks
put.description: Fields left out keep their value. language is the user's interface language, which reports are written in.

get.summary: Shipped and saved auto-ops presets, with what is enabled
get.description: Each preset lists the automations made from it and whether the shipped version is newer than the one they were made from. automationsAvailable is false while the Automations plugin is not running, and presets cannot be enabled then.

403.description: Missing ai.ops.use, or the assistant is off.

post.summary: Create an automation from a preset
post.description: Creates it through automations.access as the user: the preset's trigger with the user's changes and one ai_task step. The preset version is recorded so a newer one can be offered later.

name.description: The automation's name. Defaults to "AI · " and the title.

title.description: The report title. Defaults to the preset's title in the user's language.

400.description: Invalid changes, or Automations refused them.

403.description: Missing ai.ops.use, or the assistant is off.

503.description: The Automations plugin is not running.

post.summary: Save an auto-ops configuration as a preset
post.description: shared makes it a preset for everyone who may use auto-ops; only its creator can delete it.

400.description: Missing name or an unusable config.

403.description: Missing ai.ops.use, or the assistant is off.

delete.summary: Delete a preset the user saved

404.description: Not found, or saved by someone else.

get.summary: One auto-ops task with its report and plan
get.description: Visible to its owner and to holders of ai.ops.use. canDecide says whether the user may approve or reject its plan.

post.summary: Approve a proposed plan and run it
post.description: The owner, or a holder of ai.ops.use who can connect to every host in the plan, may approve. The plan then runs as the owner, verbatim, per host in order, stopping a host at its first failure, then its verify commands. Answers at once; poll the task for progress.

403.description: Not allowed to decide on this plan.

409.description: Not waiting for a decision, expired, or auto-ops is paused.

403.description: Not allowed to decide on this plan.

get.summary: The user's fleets with their member host ids
get.description: For the assistant's target picker. available is false while the fleets plugin is not running or the user may not read fleets.

200.description: Fleets and whether the fleets plugin is available.

403.description: Missing ai.use, or the assistant is off.

get.summary: The assistant's conversations, newest first
get.description: Shared by the floating assistant and the AI tab.

200.description: Conversations with their targets, the tokens each has used and whether a run is going on in it.

403.description: Missing ai.use, or the assistant is off.

get.summary: One assistant conversation with its messages and targets

200.description: The conversation, with the tokens it has used, how much of the model's context its latest call took and whether a run is going on in it.

delete.summary: Delete an assistant conversation and its run records
delete.description: A run going on in it is stopped first.

get.summary: Watch the run going on in an assistant conversation
get.description: The frames /ops/chat streams. Joining part way, the run's frames so far come first, then it continues live until done. With no run going on the stream is a single done frame, and the stored messages are all there is. Closing it never stops the run.

post.summary: Stop the run going on in an assistant conversation
post.description: Ends the model call and any command or CLI call it has running, and answers once the run has ended. stopped is false when there was none.

post.summary: Summarise the earlier part of an assistant conversation
post.description: What happens on its own once the context is nearly full, on request: one model call summarises all but the most recent steps, and the summary stands in for them from then on. compacted is false when the conversation is too short to gain anything.

200.description: Whether it was compacted, and the context left.

502.description: The provider could not summarise it.

post.summary: Send a message to the assistant and stream its run
post.description: Server-sent events, like /chat/stream, plus a tool_progress frame for each host as its command finishes, a targets frame when the assistant changes the targets and a client_action frame when it asks the browser to open a view. reasoning frames carry the model's thinking apart from its tokens, a usage frame follows every model call with its tokens, the context window, its source (override, provider, guess or default) and the tokens kept for the reply, and a compacted frame marks where the history was summarised to fit. The run goes on in the background: closing the stream only stops watching it, and /ops/conversations/{id}/stream picks it up again. There is no step limit; the run ends when the model answers, it is stopped, or it repeats one call with one result five times. One run at a time per conversation. hostIds become the conversation's targets; leave them out to keep the ones it has. Targets, and the tools that run commands on them, need ai.ops.use; without it a non-empty hostIds is refused and the CLI cannot exec on hosts. page is what the user is looking at.

403.description: Missing ai.use, hostIds sent without ai.ops.use, or the assistant is off.

409.description: The conversation already has a run going on.

get.summary: The asset inventory
get.description: Hosts, Proxmox guests, containers and external addresses, with their zone and counts of what was collected. Removed assets are left out unless includeRemoved is set.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches name, key or an address.

403.description: Missing ai.assets.view, or the assistant is off.

get.summary: Relations between assets
get.description: runs_on and connects_to edges with their evidence. An edge whose lastSeen is older than its source's last collection was not seen again and is stale.

get.summary: CIDR zone rules and the built-in zones

200.description: The rules, and the built-in zone names.

post.description: Rules come before the built-in ones. The most specific prefix wins, then the higher priority. Every asset not pinned is zoned again.

put.description: Fields left out keep their value.

post.description: Runs over every host the collector can connect to, or queues behind the run in progress. With no collector set yet, the caller becomes it.

get.summary: Recent collection runs
get.description: Newest first, with per-host errors and whether one is running.

get.summary: The daily collection and who collects

put.summary: Change the daily collection, the annotation, or collect as yourself
put.description: dailyTime is HH:MM in UTC. collector "me" makes the caller the collector, so collection reaches the hosts they can connect to; nobody can name another user. annotateProviderId is one of the collector's providers, null for the one their auto-ops tasks use; annotateModel null for that provider's default model.

get.summary: One asset with its facts and edges
get.description: facts is the parsed collection, by section. outgoing and incoming are its edges, each with the asset at the other end.

put.summary: Pin an asset's zone, or hand it back to the rules
put.description: A pinned zone is kept by every later collection. zone null unpins it; the rules decide again at once.

get.summary: The inventory as nodes and edges for the graph view
get.description: Live assets with their zone and annotations, and edges of the asked types between them. Containers are folded into their host (counted on it) unless containers is set; external addresses are left out unless external is set.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated edge types; all three by default.

post.description: Runs the AI annotation as the collector, over the assets that changed since their last annotation and their neighbours, or over every asset with all. Queues behind a run in progress. With no collector set yet, the caller becomes it.

get.summary: Recent annotation runs
get.description: Newest first, with assets annotated, errors and the tokens each run took, and whether one is running.

get.summary: What else fails when this asset does
get.description: Everything that runs on it or depends on it, transitively (direct and transitive), and as a weaker class what only connects to one of those. Each with the chain of edges down to this asset, and counts by importance. At most 6 hops and 300 assets per class; truncated says when that cut something off.

put.summary: Set an asset's role, importance or system yourself
put.description: Each field given is locked: annotation runs leave it alone until it is unlocked. importanceReason goes with importance.

delete.summary: Unlock a field for the annotation
delete.description: The field keeps its value until the next annotation run, which picks the asset up and fills it.
